ports.name: out
ports.label: Requests
ports.description: Sends every generated request to one entry point (usually a load balancer).

fields.label: Client timeout
fields.description: How long a client waits for a response per attempt before giving up (ms).

fields.label: Max attempts
fields.description: Total attempts per user request including retries (1 = no retries). Retries add load.

fields.label: Retry backoff
fields.description: Delay before the first retry (ms); doubles for each further retry.

fields.label: Traffic share
fields.description: Share of the workload this client group sends (%). With several client groups the shares are relative: each sends its share divided by the sum of all shares, so 60 / 30 / 10 means 60%, 30% and 10%. A single client group sends everything.

modeled: Open-loop arrivals: clients do not slow down when the system is slow

notModeled: Closed-loop users with think time

components.description: Spreads requests across the replicas of its targets (round-robin, least-connections or random). Links can filter by request type, e.g. to route reads and writes differently.

ports.name: out
ports.label: Targets
ports.description: Instances to balance across. A retry (link max attempts > 1) avoids the instance that just failed.

fields.label: Technology
fields.description: Product or managed service. A label for the design; behaviour comes from the settings below.

fields.label: Balancing policy
fields.description: How a target instance is chosen. Instances are the replicas of every linked target that carries the request type.

fields.label: Overhead
fields.description: Processing overhead added per request by the balancer itself (ms).

fields.label: Max connections
fields.description: Concurrent requests the balancer accepts; beyond this new requests are rejected.

fields.label: Rate limit
fields.description: Requests per second admitted (token bucket); excess requests are rejected (HTTP 429). Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Burst
fields.description: Bucket size: requests admitted in a burst above the rate. Empty = one second's worth.

fields.label: CPU
fields.description: vCPU per instance. Empty = not modelled. Shown on the design and used for price estimates; it does not change the simulation.

fields.label: Memory
fields.description: Memory per instance (GiB). Empty = not modelled. Shown on the design and used for price estimates; it does not change the simulation.

fields.label: Cost per hour
fields.description: Price of the balancer per hour, in USD. Illustrative default; use your provider's pricing.

modeled: Instance selection per policy across all routable replicas of linked targets (follows autoscaling)
Per-link timeout and retries that avoid the failed instance
Connection limit (rejects beyond max connections)
Optional rate limit (token bucket); excess rejected as rate_limited
notModeled: Health checks and ejection
TLS handshakes
Sticky sessions
Per-client or per-route rate limits

presets.name: HAProxy

components.description: Stateless application servers. Each replica has a worker pool and a bounded queue. Outgoing links are called in order for matching request types (e.g. reads to the cache, writes to the database). Runs on VMs, containers, Kubernetes (optional autoscaling) or as a serverless function.

ports.name: out
ports.label: Dependencies
ports.description: Downstream calls made while handling a request. Each link's request types decide which requests use it.

fields.label: Technology
fields.description: Runtime or framework. A label for the design; behaviour comes from the settings below.

fields.label: Platform
fields.description: Where it runs. VM and Docker behave the same (fixed replicas unless autoscaling is on); Kubernetes usually pairs with autoscaling (HPA); serverless runs one request per instance with cold starts and a concurrency limit.

fields.label: Replicas
fields.description: Number of identical instances. Each has its own workers and queue. With autoscaling: the starting count.

fields.label: Workers per replica
fields.description: Requests one replica processes concurrently (threads/worker processes).

fields.label: Queue limit per replica
fields.description: Requests that may wait for a free worker per replica; more are rejected (HTTP 503).

fields.label: Queue timeout
fields.description: Requests waiting longer than this for a worker are rejected (ms). Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Service time
fields.description: Handler time per request on a worker, excluding downstream calls (ms). This is an assumption unless calibrated from telemetry.

fields.label: Workers block on downstream calls
fields.description: On: a worker stays occupied while waiting for downstream calls (thread-per-request). Off: the worker is released during downstream I/O (async/event-loop servers).

fields.label: CPU
fields.description: vCPU per replica. Empty = not modelled. When set, CPU work waits for a free core while more handlers than cores want the CPU (CPU contention); below 1 (e.g. 0.5) CPU work runs proportionally slower. Service time is treated as CPU work. Serverless: one request per instance, so only values below 1 matter.

fields.label: Memory
fields.description: Memory per replica (GiB). Empty = not modelled. When set, every request a replica holds (queued, running or waiting on downstream calls) uses memory; a request that would exceed it is refused (out of memory).

fields.label: Memory per request
fields.description: Memory one in-flight request uses (MiB). Only used when memory is set.

fields.label: Memory at idle
fields.description: Memory a replica uses before any request (runtime, heap, caches) (MiB). Only used when memory is set.

fields.label: Autoscaling
fields.description: Add and remove replicas to keep utilization near the target (like a Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler). Ignored on the serverless platform.

fields.label: Min replicas
fields.description: Fewest replicas autoscaling keeps running.

fields.label: Max replicas
fields.description: Most replicas autoscaling may run.

fields.label: Target utilization
fields.description: Utilization the autoscaler aims for (share of busy workers).

fields.label: Evaluation interval
fields.description: How often the autoscaler re-evaluates (s). Scale-down waits for 3 consecutive low readings.

fields.label: Replica start-up time
fields.description: Time from the scale-up decision until a new replica takes traffic (pod scheduling, image pull, start-up, readiness).

fields.label: Concurrency limit
fields.description: Most instances (= concurrent requests) the function may run; beyond it requests are throttled.

fields.label: Cold start
fields.description: Extra time for a request that has to start a new instance (ms).

fields.label: Keep warm
fields.description: Idle time after which an instance is reclaimed (s); the next request needs a cold start.

fields.label: Cost per replica-hour
fields.description: Price of one replica (or serverless instance) per hour, in USD. Illustrative default; use your provider's pricing.

modeled: FIFO queue per replica with a size limit and a wait timeout
Worker pool per replica; service time sampled from the configured distribution
Sequential downstream calls; blocking (thread-per-request) or non-blocking I/O
Autoscaling (when on): utilization-driven replica count with evaluation interval, start-up delay and scale-down stabilization
Serverless (platform): one request per instance, cold starts, concurrency limit (throttling), idle reclaim
CPU cores (when set): service time needs a core; with fewer cores than workers, work queues for a core
Memory (when set): requests held by a replica use memory; past the limit new requests are refused
notModeled: Garbage collection pauses; OOM kills and restarts (memory is a refusal limit instead)
Parallel fan-out calls (dependencies are called one after another)
Node/cluster capacity limits for new pods, readiness probe failures
Serverless memory/CPU sizing and provisioned concurrency

presets.name: Generic service (VM)
presets.description: Fixed replicas on virtual machines, thread-per-request workers.

presets.name: Java/Spring on Docker
presets.description: Spring Boot containers with a large blocking thread pool (Tomcat-style).

presets.name: Node.js on Docker
presets.description: Single-threaded event loop per container: one handler at a time, I/O does not block it.

presets.name: Go service on Kubernetes (HPA)
presets.description: Go pods behind a Kubernetes Service with a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.

presets.name: Python service on Kubernetes (HPA)
presets.description: Gunicorn-style worker processes in pods, autoscaled by an HPA.

presets.name: Serverless function (Lambda-style)
presets.description: Function-as-a-service: an instance per concurrent request, cold starts when scaling out.

components.description: Cache-aside: reads that hit return from memory; misses continue through the 'miss' port to the data store, then optionally repopulate the cache. Writes invalidate the key.

ports.name: miss
ports.label: Miss
ports.description: Where reads go when the key is not cached (usually the database).

fields.label: Technology
fields.description: Technology label. It does not change behaviour by itself; presets set executors, command time and hit ratio to illustrative defaults for that technology.

fields.label: Hit model
fields.description: fixed_ratio: each read hits with the given probability (simplest assumption). ttl_keyspace: reads pick keys from the workload's Zipf keyspace; a key hits if it was filled less than TTL seconds ago (derives hit rate, including cold start).

fields.label: Hit ratio
fields.description: Probability a read is served from the cache (fixed_ratio model).

fields.label: TTL
fields.description: Time a filled key stays valid (ttl_keyspace model). Capacity is unbounded (no eviction).

fields.label: Populate on miss
fields.description: After a miss is served by the data store, write the value back (one extra cache operation).

fields.label: Command time
fields.description: Time to execute one cache command, excluding network (ms).

fields.label: Command executors
fields.description: Commands executed in parallel (Redis executes commands on a single thread).

fields.label: Queue limit
fields.description: Commands that may wait for an executor; more are rejected.

fields.label: Queue timeout
fields.description: Commands waiting longer than this are rejected (ms). Empty = no limit.

fields.label: CPU
fields.description: vCPU per cache node. Empty = not modelled. When set, CPU work waits for a free core while more handlers than cores want the CPU (CPU contention); below 1 (e.g. 0.5) CPU work runs proportionally slower.

fields.label: Memory
fields.description: Memory per cache node (GiB). Empty = not modelled. 80% of it holds keys. TTL model: when it is full the least recently used key is evicted. Fixed hit ratio: checked against the workload's keyspace.

fields.label: Item size
fields.description: Average size of one cached key and value, with overhead (KiB). Only used when memory is set.

fields.label: Cost per hour
fields.description: Price of the cache per hour, used for cost estimates only. Illustrative default.

modeled: Hit/miss decision per read (fixed probability or TTL over a Zipf keyspace)
Single-threaded command execution with a queue
Miss path latency added to the caller; repopulation cost
Memory (when set, TTL model): key capacity from memory and item size, LRU eviction
CPU cores (when set): commands queue for a core when executors outnumber cores
notModeled: LFU and other eviction policies; memory for the fixed-ratio model (checked, not simulated)
Thundering herd / request coalescing on misses
Replication, persistence and cluster sharding
CDN geography (edge-to-user latency belongs on the incoming link)

presets.name: Redis
presets.description: Single Redis node: commands run on one thread, sub-millisecond. Illustrative defaults.

presets.name: Valkey
presets.description: Redis-compatible; multi-threaded I/O lets a few commands proceed in parallel. Illustrative defaults.

presets.name: Memcached
presets.description: Multi-threaded, simple get/set cache. Illustrative defaults.

presets.name: CDN edge cache
presets.description: Edge cache in front of the origin: huge parallelism, a few ms per request, most reads served at the edge. Put user-to-edge latency on the incoming link. Illustrative defaults.

presets.name: Varnish
presets.description: Reverse-proxy HTTP cache in front of the application. Illustrative defaults.

components.description: Executes read and write queries on a limited number of connections per instance. Model a single relational primary, a primary with read replicas, a sharded cluster, or a leaderless store with tunable consistency; technology presets fill in illustrative defaults.

fields.label: Technology
fields.description: Technology label. It does not change behaviour by itself; presets set the values below to illustrative defaults for that technology.

fields.label: Max connections per instance
fields.description: Queries executing concurrently on one instance (connection pool size / backend workers). Every primary and replica in every shard has its own limit.

fields.label: Read query time
fields.description: Execution time of a read query on one instance (ms).

fields.label: Write query time
fields.description: Execution time of a write query including commit (ms).

fields.label: Read replicas
fields.description: Read-only copies per shard. Reads are spread round-robin over the primary and its replicas; writes always go to the primary. Replication lag is not modeled.

fields.label: Shards (partitions)
fields.description: Partitions of the data, each with its own primary (and replicas). Requests are routed by hashing the key, so popular keys concentrate load on one shard.

fields.label: Replication factor
fields.description: Copies of each item kept by a leaderless or consensus store (e.g. Cassandra, DynamoDB-style, distributed SQL). Combined with the consistency level it decides how many replica responses an operation waits for.

fields.label: Consistency level
fields.description: Replica responses an operation waits for when the replication factor is above 1: one, a majority (quorum) or all. Latency becomes the k-th fastest of the replicas.

fields.label: Throughput limit per shard
fields.description: Provisioned throughput per shard (operations/s, bursts up to one second's worth). Requests above it are throttled. Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Wait queue limit
fields.description: Queries that may wait for a connection on one instance; more are rejected.

fields.label: Acquire timeout
fields.description: Connection acquire timeout (ms). Queries waiting longer are rejected. Empty = no limit.

fields.label: CPU
fields.description: vCPU per instance. Empty = not modelled. When set, CPU work waits for a free core while more handlers than cores want the CPU (CPU contention); below 1 (e.g. 0.5) CPU work runs proportionally slower. Only the CPU share of each query needs a core.

fields.label: CPU share of query time
fields.description: Share of query time that needs a CPU core; the rest is I/O, locks and network. Only used when CPU is set.

fields.label: Memory
fields.description: Memory per instance (GiB). Empty = not modelled. With a working set, 75% of it is buffer cache: reads of data that does not fit go to disk.

fields.label: Hot working set
fields.description: Size of the data that is read often (GiB), across all shards. With memory set, the share of reads served from memory is min(1, 75% of memory / working set per shard).

fields.label: Disk read time
fields.description: Extra time of a read that misses the buffer cache and goes to disk (ms).

fields.label: Storage
fields.description: Disk per instance (GiB). Empty = not modelled. Checked against the data size: each instance stores its shard's data.

fields.label: Data size
fields.description: Total data stored (GiB), across all shards. Used to check storage.

fields.label: Cost per instance-hour
fields.description: Price of one instance (primary or replica, per shard) per hour, used for cost estimates only. Illustrative default; use your own price.

modeled: Connection limit with a bounded wait queue and acquire timeout, per instance
Separate read/write query time distributions
Read replicas: reads round-robin over primary and replicas, writes to the primary
Key-hash sharding; a skewed (Zipf) keyspace creates hot shards
Replication factor + consistency level: latency is the k-th fastest of RF replicas
Provisioned throughput per shard; excess requests are throttled
CPU cores (when set): the CPU share of each query needs a core; queries queue for cores
Buffer cache (memory and working set set): reads of data that does not fit pay a disk read
Storage (with a data size): checked per instance
notModeled: Locks, MVCC contention, write I/O and checkpoints, eviction dynamics of the buffer cache
Replication lag and stale reads; failover and leader election
Replica load in leaderless writes (an operation holds one connection, not RF)
Cross-shard queries and transactions, rebalancing, query planning

presets.name: PostgreSQL
presets.description: Single PostgreSQL primary behind an application connection pool. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: PostgreSQL + 2 read replicas
presets.description: Primary for writes, two streaming replicas that share the reads. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: MySQL
presets.description: Single MySQL (InnoDB) primary. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: SQL Server
presets.description: Single SQL Server instance; the hourly price includes a licence. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: CockroachDB-style distributed SQL
presets.description: Three ranges/shards, each replicated three times with quorum (Raft) writes: survives a node loss, pays a consensus round trip. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: MongoDB replica set
presets.description: Primary plus two secondaries; reads use secondaries (secondaryPreferred). Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: MongoDB sharded cluster
presets.description: Four shards, each a replica set (primary + two secondaries), routed by shard key. A skewed key distribution makes one shard hot. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: Cassandra
presets.description: Six token ranges, replication factor 3, QUORUM reads and writes. LSM storage makes writes cheaper than reads. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: DynamoDB-style key-value store
presets.description: Managed key-value store with four partitions and provisioned throughput per partition; requests above it are throttled. The hourly price stands in for provisioned capacity. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

presets.name: Elasticsearch
presets.description: Three primary shards with one replica each; searches are slower than key lookups and indexing is the expensive write. Defaults are illustrative assumptions, not vendor benchmarks.

components.description: A third-party service you call but do not operate (payments, email, SMS, identity, LLM inference, object storage). Each call takes the provider's response time, may fail, and may be rejected by the provider's rate or concurrency limit.

fields.label: Kind of service
fields.description: Kind of provider. A label only; presets set latency, error rate, limits and price to illustrative defaults.

fields.label: Response time
fields.description: Time the provider takes to answer one call, excluding network to it (ms).

fields.label: Error rate
fields.description: Share of calls the provider fails (5xx / errors), after its response time.

fields.label: Rate limit
fields.description: Calls per second the provider accepts (bursts up to one second's worth); more are rejected as rate limited. Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Concurrency limit
fields.description: Calls that may be in flight at once; more are rejected as throttled. Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Cost per million calls
fields.description: Price per million calls, used for cost estimates only. Illustrative default.

modeled: Response time sampled from the configured distribution
Random provider errors at the configured rate
Provider rate limit (token bucket) and concurrency limit; excess calls fail immediately
Price per million calls for cost estimates
notModeled: Provider-side queueing and degradation under your load
Retry-After headers and provider-side backoff
Regional outages (use a fault to inject one)

presets.name: Payments API
presets.description: Card payment provider: a few hundred ms per charge, rare errors, per-account rate limit. Usually priced per transaction amount, so no per-call price is set. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

presets.name: Email API
presets.description: Transactional email sending. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

presets.name: SMS API
presets.description: SMS / messaging provider: slower and pricier per call. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

presets.name: Identity provider
presets.description: OAuth/OIDC identity provider for token checks and logins. Usually priced per active user, so no per-call price is set. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

presets.name: LLM inference API
presets.description: Hosted model inference: seconds per call with a heavy tail, tight rate and concurrency limits, noticeable error rate. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

presets.name: Object storage (S3-compatible)
presets.description: Object GETs from S3-compatible storage: tens of ms, very high limits. Numbers are illustrative assumptions, not a provider's published figures.

components.description: Asynchronous messaging (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS-style). Producers get an acknowledgement after publishing; consumers process messages in the background and call the outgoing links. Absorbs spikes as backlog (lag) instead of rejecting requests.

ports.name: in
ports.label: Publish
ports.description: Messages published by producers (the caller gets an ack, not the result).

ports.name: out
ports.label: Consumers
ports.description: Downstream calls each consumer makes per message, in order, for matching request types.

fields.label: Technology
fields.description: Product or managed service. A label for the design; behaviour comes from the settings below.

fields.label: Partitions
fields.description: Partitions (Kafka) or shards: at most one consumer works per partition, so effective consumers = min(consumers, partitions). Set it high for brokers without partitions.

fields.label: Consumers
fields.description: Concurrent consumers processing messages (consumer instances x threads).

fields.label: Max backlog
fields.description: Messages the queue holds; publishes beyond it are rejected (queue_full). Empty = unbounded.

fields.label: Publish (ack) time
fields.description: Time for the broker to acknowledge a publish (ms): what the producer waits.

fields.label: Consumer time
fields.description: Consumer handling time per message before its downstream calls (ms).

fields.label: Max deliveries
fields.description: Delivery attempts per message; after the last failure it goes to the dead-letter queue.

fields.label: Brokers
fields.description: Broker nodes in the cluster (used for cost; throughput is set by consumers and partitions).

fields.label: CPU
fields.description: vCPU per broker. Empty = not modelled. Shown on the design and used for price estimates; it does not change the simulation.

fields.label: Memory
fields.description: Memory per broker (GiB). Empty = not modelled. Shown on the design and used for price estimates; it does not change the simulation.

fields.label: Storage
fields.description: Disk per broker (GiB). Empty = not modelled. Shown on the design and used for price estimates; it does not change the simulation.

fields.label: Cost per broker-hour
fields.description: Price of one broker per hour, in USD. Illustrative default; use your provider's pricing.

modeled: Publish acknowledgement latency and a bounded backlog (rejects when full)
FIFO consumption by min(consumers, partitions) parallel consumers
Redelivery of failed messages up to max deliveries, then dead-lettering
Backlog (lag), consumer utilization and message age
notModeled: Per-partition ordering and key-based partition skew
Broker replication, disk and network throughput limits
Consumer rebalancing, visibility timeouts and duplicate delivery

presets.name: Kafka
presets.description: Partitioned log: consumer parallelism is capped by partitions; acks=all publish latency.

presets.name: RabbitMQ
presets.description: Message broker with competing consumers on a queue.

presets.name: SQS-style queue
presets.description: Managed HTTP queue: slower publishes, effectively unbounded backlog (illustrative numbers).

presets.name: Pub/Sub-style topic
presets.description: Managed publish/subscribe with push or pull subscribers (illustrative numbers).

presets.name: NATS
presets.description: Lightweight messaging (JetStream for persistence) with very low publish latency.

presets.name: Redis Streams
presets.description: Append-only stream with consumer groups, in memory.

edgeFields.label: Request types
edgeFields.description: Request types carried by this link. Used for routing (e.g. reads to cache, writes to DB).

edgeFields.label: Network latency (one way)
edgeFields.description: One-way network latency in ms, applied to the request and again to the response.

edgeFields.label: Timeout
edgeFields.description: Per-attempt time the caller waits before giving up (ms). Empty = wait indefinitely.

edgeFields.label: Max attempts
edgeFields.description: Total attempts including retries (1 = no retries). Bounded to prevent retry storms from running away.

edgeFields.label: Retry backoff
edgeFields.description: Base backoff before a retry (ms); doubles on each further retry.

edgeFields.label: Call order
edgeFields.description: Call order when a service calls several dependencies for the same request (lower first).

workloadFields.label: Warm-up
workloadFields.description: Initial period excluded from summary statistics (s)

workloadFields.label: Read ratio
workloadFields.description: Fraction of requests that are reads

workloadFields.label: Arrival process
workloadFields.description: poisson: random (exponential) inter-arrivals; deterministic: evenly spaced

workloadFields.label: Traffic pattern
workloadFields.description: Shape of the offered load over time

workloadFields.label: Distinct keys
workloadFields.description: Number of distinct keys requests touch (used by TTL cache models)

workloadFields.label: Key skew (Zipf s)
